citation: Schwander F, Kopf-Bolanz KA, Buri C, et al. A Dose-Response Strategy Reveals Differences between Normal-Weight and Obese Men in Their Metabolic and Inflammatory Responses to a High-Fat Meal123. The Journal of Nutrition. 2014;144(10):1517-1523.
protocol: High-fat meal (60.5% energy from fat; bread, palm fat and other items, grams in Table 1) at 500, 1000 and 1500 kcal on three occasions, crossover; meals differ only in size. Blood at 0, 1, 2, 4, 6 h.
population: 19 normal-weight (BMI 20-25) and 18 obese (BMI >30) men; Switzerland. Table 3 lists normal-weight n = 19 and obese n = 17.

reports.where: Table 3: net iAUC over 6 h for each dose and group

note: The only dose-response here: one fat-rich meal at three sizes in the same men, so it tests how the model's insulin output scales with meal size. Licence element is the ASN/J Nutr open-access licence, not CC. The AUCs are net incremental over 6 h with sparse sampling. Only in figures: insulin concentration time course. Meal kinds: fat load, mixed meal.
